{{short description|American food scientist}}
'''Alina Surmacka Szczesniak''' (July 8, 1925 – July 23, 2016) was a Polish-born American [[food science|food scientist]] best known for her contributions to food texture.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/lohud/obituary.aspx?n=alina-surmacka-szczesniak&pid=180813430&fhid=27182|title=Alina Surmacka Szczesniak's Obituary on The Journal News|work=legacy.com|accessdate=12 August 2016}}</ref>

==Education and career==

<!-- Commented out: [[File:Alina Surmacka Szczesniak.jpg|thumb|right|alt=Szcześniak receiving plaque (2002)|Szcześniak receiving plaque (2002)]] -->
She was the daughter of Wladysław Surmacki, who was to be President of the [[International Federation of Surveyors]] (FIG) in 1942 but did not survive the Second World War.
In 2002, Szcześniak received the plaque of Honorary President of FIG on behalf of her father.<ref>{{Cite web |title=FIG General Assembly - Minutes - 2002 |url=http://www.fig.net/printpage.asp?page=http://www.fig.net/organisation/general_assembly/agendas_and_minutes/2002/minutes.asp |access-date=2022-04-12 |website=www.fig.net}}</ref>

Szcześniak attended [[Bryn Mawr College]] as a foreign student after the [[Second World War]], which she spent in her native [[Poland]].

Szcześniak earned her graduate degree in [[food technology]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], then worked for [[General Foods]] in the field of [[food chemistry]], focusing on texture studies. She worked at General Foods from 1952 until her 1986 retirement, where she retired as a principal scientist.

Szcześniak developed the now-standard Sensory Texture Profile Analysis,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Texture Profile Analysis |url=http://texturetechnologies.com/resources/texture-profile-analysis |access-date=2022-04-12 |website=texturetechnologies.com}}</ref> which analyzes, quantifies and places in correct sequence all textural properties perceived from the moment a piece of food is placed in the mouth until the last particle is swallowed.

In 1969, Szcześniak was a founding editor of the ''Journal of Texture Studies''<ref name=":0" /> and served for 10 years in that role.

==Awards and honours==
In 1985, Szcześniak became the first woman to receive the [[Nicholas Appert Award]], the highest honor bestowed upon its members by the [[Institute of Food Technologists]] (IFT). It commended her ''pioneering work on food texture that led to its recognition as an important quality attribute affecting consumer acceptance and to its organization as a subdiscipline of food science.'' She is the only woman thus far to ever win the Nicholas Appert Award. Dr Szcześniak was elected an IFT Fellow in 1981.
